variations.name: Shelf-life extension coatings, packaging & treatments
variations.description: Edible coatings, ripening-control treatments (e.g., 1-MCP), and active packaging slow respiration and moisture loss so produce survives longer in transit and on shelf, cutting spoilage-driven waste and the emissions embodied in lost food.

companies.name: Apeel Sciences
companies.what: Plant-derived edible coatings applied at packhouses that extend shelf life of avocados, citrus, cucumbers and more by days to weeks.
companies.signal: Raised ~$640M total incl. $250M Series E (2021, ~$2B valuation); deployed with major US/EU retailers; restructured 2023-24 amid slower-than-hoped commercialization

companies.name: Hazel Technologies
companies.what: Drop-in sachets and packaging inserts that release vapor-phase ripening inhibitors inside produce boxes during transit.
companies.signal: ~$110M raised through Series C; used by hundreds of produce suppliers across dozens of crops

companies.name: AgroFresh
companies.what: Dominant supplier of 1-MCP post-harvest freshness treatments (SmartFresh) used on a large share of the world's stored apples, plus coatings and digital tools.
companies.signal: NASDAQ-listed until taken private by Paine Schwartz Partners (completed 2023); decades of global deployment

companies.name: Mori
companies.what: Silk-protein (fibroin) edible coating with FDA GRAS status applied to produce and proteins to slow spoilage.
companies.signal: Raised >$80M venture funding (Series B 2022); commercial pilots with US produce and protein processors

companies.name: Ryp Labs
companies.what: StixFresh produce stickers that release natural antimicrobial vapors to delay mold and over-ripening on individual fruit.
companies.signal: Venture/grant-backed; retail and packer pilots in US and Europe

companies.name: RipeLocker
companies.what: Patented low-atmospheric-pressure storage containers that hold berries, hops, and flowers in suspended animation for weeks.
companies.signal: Commercial trials with major berry and hop shippers; named alongside Apeel/Hazel as a category leader

companies.name: Sufresca
companies.what: Israeli developer of invisible, washable edible coatings tailored per-crop (cucumbers, peppers, citrus).
companies.signal: Seed-stage; pilots with European produce packers

companies.name: Saveggy
companies.what: Swedish plant-based coating replacing plastic shrink-wrap on cucumbers and peppers.
companies.signal: Early commercial rollout with Nordic retailer ICA; seed/EU-grant funded

companies.name: Xampla
companies.what: Cambridge spinout making Morro-brand natural polymer coatings and films from plant protein as edible/compostable barriers for food.
companies.signal: Raised ~$20M+; commercial partnerships incl. Huhtamaki and food brands

variations.name: Surplus food marketplaces, redistribution & dynamic pricing
variations.description: Apps and B2B platforms match soon-to-expire or surplus food with discount buyers, charities, or secondary channels — and dynamically mark down prices — so edible food gets eaten instead of landfilled.

companies.name: Too Good To Go
companies.what: Consumer app selling 'surprise bags' of unsold food from restaurants, bakeries, and grocers at steep discounts; the category's global leader.
companies.signal: EUR 194M revenue and positive EBIT in 2024; ~100M+ registered users; reported mid-2025 to be weighing a EUR 200-300M growth round

companies.name: Flashfood
companies.what: App platform grocers use to sell near-dated meat, produce, and dairy at ~50% off for in-store pickup.
companies.signal: Partnered with thousands of stores (Meijer and other chains) across North America; 100M+ lbs of food diverted

companies.name: Misfits Market
companies.what: Online grocer built on 'ugly' and surplus produce and short-coded pantry goods delivered to consumers.
companies.signal: Raised $526.5M (SoftBank, Accel, Valor); acquired rival Imperfect Foods in 2022

companies.name: Imperfect Foods
companies.what: Pioneer of imperfect-produce subscription boxes; consolidated into Misfits Market as standalone economics proved hard.
companies.signal: Acquired by Misfits Market (2022) after raising ~$229M; brand retained

companies.name: Phenix
companies.what: French anti-waste app plus donation logistics that routes retailer surplus to consumers and charities across Western Europe.
companies.signal: B Corp; thousands of partner merchants in France/Spain/Portugal/Italy/Belgium; raised ~EUR 15M+

companies.name: OLIO
companies.what: Neighbor-to-neighbor and store-to-community sharing app where volunteers redistribute retailer surplus for free.
companies.signal: Raised ~$43M Series B (2021, VNV Global); millions of users; Tesco volunteer partnership

companies.name: Goodr
companies.what: Atlanta-based surplus-food logistics company routing edible surplus from airports, stadiums, and corporates to nonprofits, with waste audits.
companies.signal: Venture-backed (raised ~$8M+); clients include major airports and arenas

companies.name: Spoiler Alert
companies.what: B2B private marketplace where CPG brands liquidate excess and short-dated inventory to discount/secondary channels.
companies.signal: Raised ~$32M; used by Kraft Heinz, Nestlé, Danone and other top food brands

companies.name: Wasteless
companies.what: AI dynamic-pricing engine that marks down perishables by remaining shelf life via electronic shelf labels and POS integration.
companies.signal: Live in ~1,000 stores across 18 grocery chains in US/Europe; users report ~40% waste reduction

companies.name: Full Harvest
companies.what: B2B marketplace selling farms' off-grade and surplus produce directly to food & beverage manufacturers.
companies.signal: Raised ~$23M Series B (Telus Ventures); still operating as of 2025 industry coverage

variations.name: Upcycled ingredients & byproduct valorization
variations.description: Turns high-volume food-processing byproducts (spent grain, okara, fruit peels, coffee waste, veg trim) into flours, proteins, snacks, and functional actives, capturing the nutrition and embedded emissions of food that would otherwise be discarded.

companies.name: Upcycled Foods Inc. (ReGrained)
companies.what: Converts brewers' spent grain into SuperGrain+ flour and supplies a B2B upcycled-ingredient platform; co-founded the Upcycled Food Association certification.
companies.signal: B Corp; ingredient partnerships with major bakeries/CPGs; certification scheme now covers 500+ products industry-wide

companies.name: Renewal Mill
companies.what: Mills okara (soymilk byproduct) and oat-milk solids into gluten-free flours and baking mixes for retail and bakery B2B.
companies.signal: B Corp; products in national retail and on Amazon; active as of 2025

companies.name: Matriark Foods
companies.what: Upcycles farm surplus and fresh-cut vegetable trim into low-sodium sauces and broths for foodservice and institutions.
companies.signal: Sold into schools, hospitals, and city institutional buyers; Upcycled Certified

companies.name: RIND Snacks
companies.what: Dried whole-fruit snacks that keep the nutrient-dense peel on, diverting peel waste from processing.
companies.signal: Raised ~$9.5M Series A (2022); national retail incl. Whole Foods

companies.name: Kaffe Bueno
companies.what: Danish biorefinery extracting active ingredients for cosmetics, nutrition, and functional food from spent coffee grounds.
companies.signal: Raised ~EUR 6M+; supplies ingredients to personal-care and food customers

companies.name: Agrain (Circular Food Technology)
companies.what: Danish brand turning brewers' spent grain into flours, granola, and snack products at commercial bakery scale.
companies.signal: Sold in Danish retail/foodservice; EU circular-economy grant backing

companies.name: Toast Brewing
companies.what: UK brewery replacing part of its brewing barley with surplus bakery bread, donating profits to food-waste charities.
companies.signal: B Corp; UK supermarket listings; brewed with millions of bread slices to date

companies.name: EverGrain
companies.what: AB InBev subsidiary industrializing barley protein (EverPro) and fiber from the brewer's 1.4M tonnes/yr of spent grain.
companies.signal: $100M commercial plant on AB InBev's St. Louis campus (2022); Upcycled Certified; partnerships with Nestlé and Post

companies.name: Do Good Foods
companies.what: Built capital-intensive plants converting grocery food waste into chicken feed to sell 'carbon-reduced' chicken at retail.
companies.signal: Filed for Chapter 11 in June 2023 just two years after launch despite ~$169M financing; had diverted 27M lbs of food waste

variations.white_space: Consumer 'story brands' keep stalling on distribution and price premiums, and capex-heavy vertically integrated models are fragile (Do Good Foods' 2023 bankruptcy is the cautionary tale); the credible opening is B2B ingredients that win on cost and functionality at parity, co-located with large processors for free feedstock (the EverGrain model), rather than selling the upcycled story at a markup.

variations.name: Retail / kitchen waste analytics & demand forecasting (inventory AI)
variations.description: AI cameras, smart scales, and forecasting software show commercial kitchens and grocers exactly what they over-produce or over-order so they buy and prep less — preventing waste before it happens, the highest-value intervention in the hierarchy.

companies.name: Afresh Technologies
companies.what: AI ordering and inventory platform purpose-built for fresh departments at grocery chains.
companies.signal: Raised $34M (Apr 2026, Just Climate); live in 12,500+ store departments; 70% YoY revenue growth in 2025; ~8B ordering decisions/yr

companies.name: Crisp
companies.what: Retail data collaboration platform unifying POS/supply data for CPGs and grocers; added automated perishable ordering by buying Shelf Engine.
companies.signal: Raised ~$112M total; acquired Shelf Engine March 2025

companies.name: Shelf Engine
companies.what: Automated demand forecasting and guaranteed-sale ordering for highly perishable grocery SKUs.
companies.signal: Raised ~$58M, downsized in 2022, then acquired by Crisp in March 2025 — consolidation marker for standalone forecasting startups

companies.name: Winnow
companies.what: Computer-vision scales under kitchen bins that identify and cost every item thrown away in hotel and foodservice kitchens.
companies.signal: ~$20M Series C (Ingka/IKEA among investors); 3,500+ sites in 94 countries; clients (Hilton, Accor, Marriott, IKEA) saving $100M+/yr; IKEA cut food waste 54%

companies.name: Leanpath
companies.what: The original food-waste tracking hardware/software for institutional kitchens (founded 2004), now with photo-based AI.
companies.signal: Deployed in 40+ countries with Sodexo, Aramark, Google cafeterias

companies.name: Orbisk
companies.what: Fully automated camera-over-bin monitor that recognizes wasted ingredients without staff input.
companies.signal: EUR 8M+ Series A (Dec 2024); expanding to US incl. Carnival Cruise Line deployments in 2025

companies.name: KITRO
companies.what: Swiss automated food-waste measurement (camera + scale) for hotels and staff restaurants in DACH and beyond.
companies.signal: Raised ~CHF 5M+; deployments across European hospitality groups

companies.name: RELEX Solutions
companies.what: Finnish retail supply-chain planning suite whose forecasting/replenishment measurably cuts grocery spoilage at chain scale.
companies.signal: Raised $568M (2022) at ~$5.7B valuation; hundreds of major grocery customers globally

companies.name: Blue Yonder
companies.what: Panasonic-owned supply-chain software giant providing demand forecasting and fresh replenishment for the world's largest grocers.
companies.signal: Acquired by Panasonic (2021, ~$8B); incumbent standard in grocery planning

variations.name: Post-harvest loss reduction & off-grid cold chain / storage
variations.description: Solar-powered cold rooms, milk chillers, modular packhouses, and hermetic storage protect crops in the hours and weeks after harvest in regions without reliable grid power, where 30-40% of food can be lost before it ever reaches a market.

companies.name: ColdHubs
companies.what: Nigerian network of pay-per-crate solar walk-in cold rooms installed in produce markets and farm clusters.
companies.signal: Operating ~50+ hubs; announced 2025 expansion of 45 new hubs incl. five 100-ton units

companies.name: SokoFresh
companies.what: Kenyan cooling-as-a-service: mobile solar cold rooms plus market-linkage aggregation for smallholders and avocado exporters.
companies.signal: Cut user spoilage to ~2%; Acumen PEII+ backed; raising ~$1.5M bridge with >$10M Series A planned for 2027

companies.name: Ecozen
companies.what: Indian maker of Ecofrost solar cold rooms (with thermal-battery storage) and solar pumps; among the largest agri-cooling fleets in India.
companies.signal: Thousands of systems deployed; named a leading global solar cold-storage player; venture and debt funded through Series C-stage

companies.name: Inficold
companies.what: Indian thermal-energy-storage retrofits that let cold rooms and bulk milk coolers run on solar without batteries.
companies.signal: 100+ installations across India; national cleantech awards

companies.name: InspiraFarms Cooling
companies.what: Modular pre-cooling and packhouse cold rooms for export horticulture in East and Southern Africa, financeable as energy-efficient assets.
companies.signal: DFI-backed; installed with major flower/veg exporters in Kenya, Rwanda, Ethiopia

companies.name: GrainPro
companies.what: Hermetic storage pioneer (Cocoons, GrainSafe bags) that suffocates pests and stops mold in stored grain without chemicals.
companies.signal: Products used in 100+ countries for 30+ years across smallholder and commodity storage

companies.name: Promethean Power Systems
companies.what: Thermal-battery rapid milk chillers that work on intermittent grid power at Indian village dairy collection points.
companies.signal: Deployed across thousands of rural collection centers with Indian dairy processors

companies.name: Vestergaard (ZeroFly)
companies.what: Insecticide-incorporated ZeroFly storage bags protecting smallholder grain from storage pests, sold via humanitarian and agri channels.
companies.signal: Global health/agri incumbent; ZeroFly distributed across Africa and Asia

variations.white_space: The physics is solved; the economics aren't — smallholders can't pay upfront for cold rooms, so deployment still leans on donors and DFIs and few players reach VC scale. The opening is cooling-as-a-service with embedded finance (pay-per-crate, loss-linked or carbon-linked payments) bundled with market aggregation, the model SokoFresh and ColdHubs are proving, plus first-loss capital to crowd in commercial debt.

variations.name: Anaerobic digestion & composting of food / organic waste
variations.description: Anaerobic digesters and composting facilities convert unavoidable food waste into renewable natural gas, electricity, and soil amendments, displacing fossil fuels and avoiding the landfill methane that makes food waste a top climate problem.

companies.name: Vanguard Renewables
companies.what: US leader in farm-based co-digestion of food & beverage waste with dairy manure into RNG, with end-to-end depackaging and organics logistics.
companies.signal: Acquired by BlackRock Real Assets (2022, reported ~$700M); building out national pipeline incl. new Minnesota advanced AD facility (2026)

companies.name: Divert
companies.what: Retail-focused wasted-food processing: recovers edible food, then converts the rest to RNG at integrated facilities serving grocery chains.
companies.signal: $1B infrastructure agreement with Enbridge (2023, ~$1B valuation); $90M+ Nuveen investment (2025); partners incl. Raley's and US Cold Storage

companies.name: Bioenergy Devco
companies.what: Develops and operates anaerobic digestion campuses (e.g., Maryland Bioenergy Center) digesting food processing and organics streams.
companies.signal: Raised $100M+ (Irradiant Partners); operating flagship Seaford/Jessup facilities

companies.name: Anaergia
companies.what: Supplies advanced AD technology (mixers, biogas upgrading, organics extraction from MSW) and operates plants globally.
companies.signal: TSX-listed; recapitalized 2024 after financial strain; C$8M follow-on technology contract from Vanguard Renewables (Apr 2026)

companies.name: Generate Upcycle
companies.what: Generate Capital's organics arm owning/operating AD and industrial composting assets (incl. Atlas Organics sites) across North America.
companies.signal: Backed by Generate's $10B+ sustainable-infrastructure balance sheet; multiple operating organics facilities

companies.name: HomeBiogas
companies.what: Prefab household and commercial-kitchen biodigesters producing cooking gas and fertilizer from food scraps, strong in off-grid markets.
companies.signal: Tel Aviv-listed (TASE); tens of thousands of systems in 100+ countries

companies.name: WM (Waste Management)
companies.what: North America's largest waste company; CORe facilities slurry commercial food waste for codigestion and it operates large compost sites.
companies.signal: Multi-billion sustainability capex program incl. organics processing expansion

companies.name: Veolia
companies.what: Global environmental utility operating food-waste anaerobic digestion and organics recycling plants across Europe, UK, and Asia.
companies.signal: EUR 40B+ revenue incumbent with long-standing AD fleet

companies.name: Denali
companies.what: Largest US organics-recycling specialist, collecting and processing food waste, depackaging, and land-applying/composting at national scale.
companies.signal: PE-backed roll-up processing ~10M tons of organics annually

variations.name: Home & consumer food-waste tech (countertop digesters/composters)
variations.description: Countertop and under-sink appliances dry, grind, or microbially ferment household food scraps into feedstock, compost precursor, or animal-feed ingredients, diverting kitchen waste from landfill where it would generate methane.

companies.name: Mill Industries
companies.what: Subscription kitchen bin (from Nest's co-founder) that dries and grinds scraps into shelf-stable grounds with a mail-back pathway into chicken feed.
companies.signal: Raised ~$200M total incl. ~$100M Series C (2023); expanded into workplace/B2B channels

companies.name: Lomi (Pela)
companies.what: Best-known countertop electric 'composter' grinding and dehydrating scraps into soil amendment; Lomi 2 added smart features.
companies.signal: Hundreds of thousands of units sold DTC; piloting at-home recycling and curbside collection programs in Canada

companies.name: Vitamix (FoodCycler)
companies.what: Appliance incumbent whose FoodCycler line anchors municipally subsidized household diversion programs across Canadian towns.
companies.signal: Deployed via 100+ municipal pilot/subsidy programs in Canada

companies.name: Reencle
companies.what: Korean microbial fermentation home composter that digests scraps continuously with a living culture rather than just drying them.
companies.signal: Large Korean install base; expanded US DTC/retail sales

companies.name: Sepura Home
companies.what: Under-sink appliance that automatically separates food scraps from sink waste into a sealed collection bin, replacing the garbage disposal.
companies.signal: Shipping in North America; CES-awarded hardware startup

companies.name: GEME
companies.what: European-market microbial countertop composter positioning on true aerobic fermentation versus dry-grind rivals.
companies.signal: DTC sales across EU; competes head-on with Lomi/Mill/Reencle

variations.white_space: Net climate benefit is contested — drying isn't composting, devices embed energy and materials, and output often still lands in the trash — while $300-1,000 price points cap the addressable market. The defensible openings are municipally subsidized diversion where curbside organics collection is impractical (the FoodCycler model) and verified end-use of output (Mill's feed pathway), not more DTC gadgets.

variations.name: Freshness sensing, smart labels & shelf-life prediction
variations.description: Biosensors, time-temperature labels, and NIR scanners measure how fresh food actually is — instead of relying on conservative printed dates — enabling dynamic expiry, first-expired-first-out routing, and fewer premature discards across the cold chain and at home.

companies.name: Strella Biotech
companies.what: Ethylene biosensors in controlled-atmosphere storage that predict ripeness so packers open and ship the ripest rooms first.
companies.signal: $11.3M raised (latest $5.6M, Feb 2024; GV among investors); monitors a meaningful share of US apple storage

companies.name: Mimica
companies.what: Touch-based 'bumpy when spoiled' caps and labels whose gel decays at the same rate as the food, giving accurate tactile expiry.
companies.signal: UK startup; award-winning; pilots with dairy, juice, and meat brands

companies.name: Evigence
companies.what: Time-temperature freshness indicators printed on packs that visually show remaining real shelf life through the supply chain.
companies.signal: Deployed with major foodservice and CPG customers in US/EU

companies.name: OneThird
companies.what: Handheld/inline NIR scanners plus AI that predict remaining shelf life of avocados, berries, and tomatoes at DCs and stores.
companies.signal: Dutch startup working with major grocery distribution centers; venture/EU funded

companies.name: Tive
companies.what: Real-time multi-sensor shipment trackers and platform that catch cold-chain excursions before loads are lost.
companies.signal: Raised ~$82M total (Series B $54M, 2022); thousands of shipper customers

companies.name: Sensitech
companies.what: Carrier-owned market leader in cold-chain monitoring (TempTale) used across global perishable logistics.
companies.signal: Decades-deployed incumbent within Carrier's $20B+ portfolio

companies.name: DeltaTrak
companies.what: Long-standing supplier of temperature data loggers and FlashLink real-time trackers for produce and protein shippers.
companies.signal: 30+ year incumbent across North American produce logistics

variations.white_space: Adoption is throttled by static date-label regulation and by per-unit label costs that don't fit penny-margin packaged food, so most players stay pilot-scale point solutions; EU date-marking reform or retailer shrink mandates tying markdowns to measured freshness (pairing sensing with dynamic pricing engines like Wasteless) would crack the market open.

variations.name: Insect bioconversion of food waste
variations.description: Black soldier fly larvae and mealworms eat food waste and processing byproducts and are harvested as protein for animal feed, pet food, and aquaculture plus frass fertilizer, valorizing streams unsuitable for human consumption.

companies.name: Protix
companies.what: Operates the world's first industrial-scale black soldier fly facility (Bergen op Zoom, NL) producing feed and pet-food protein.
companies.signal: Strategic investment and US joint venture with Tyson Foods (2023) to build a larger US plant

companies.name: InnovaFeed
companies.what: French BSF producer co-locating plants with grain processors (ADM in Decatur, IL) to use byproduct feedstock and waste heat.
companies.signal: Raised ~EUR 250M+ (Series D); cited as the sector's healthiest survivor due to staged scale-up

companies.name: Better Origin
companies.what: Containerized AI-run X1 insect mini-farms that convert food waste into larvae feed on-site at UK egg farms.
companies.signal: Deployed with Morrisons' egg supply chain; venture-backed (Fly Ventures et al.)

companies.name: Goterra
companies.what: Australian robotic BSF modules ('MIBs') placed at supermarkets and waste sites to process food waste autonomously.
companies.signal: Contracts with Woolworths and Australian councils; venture-backed

companies.name: Entocycle
companies.what: Sells BSF breeding technology and turnkey farm design so waste companies can build their own insect bioconversion capacity.
companies.signal: London demonstration facility; UK government grant backing

companies.name: Ynsect
companies.what: French mealworm pioneer that built a giant vertical insect 'farm of the future' (Amiens) for feed and food proteins.
companies.signal: Raised $600M+ but entered receivership Mar 2025 and judicial liquidation Dec 2025; flagship plant closed — only EUR 656k revenue in 2023 vs EUR 80M losses

companies.name: AgriProtein
companies.what: South African early mover feeding true mixed food waste to BSF at industrial scale for feed protein.
companies.signal: Raised ~$105M at ~$200M valuation, then collapsed (~2021) — variable waste substrate at scale proved unworkable

variations.white_space: The two biggest players failed on unit economics — insect meal costs 2-10x fish/soy meal and EU/US feed rules bar most true post-consumer food waste as substrate, which strands the cheapest feedstock. Openings: small modular on-farm/at-store units that skip central logistics (Better Origin, Goterra), co-location with processors for clean byproduct streams (InnovaFeed), and regulatory change permitting former-foodstuffs substrates.
